bull.probability_evidence: Operating margin is 28.5% TTM (+10.0pp over 5y), ROIC 16.1% (+3.2pp) and gross margin 48.2%, all rising, while every multiple sits below its own 5-year minimum (P/E 14.9x vs a 20.5x floor) and FCF yield is 5.66% (fact sheet Quality/Valuation); beta 0.69 and RSI 28.4 suggest much of the USI integration/leverage fear is already priced (fact sheet 'Other'/'News & sentiment'; evaluation Bull case). base.probability_evidence: EV/EBITDA (12.2x) already sits close to the peer median (12.4x, -2%) even as the P/E discount (14.9x vs a 20.3x peer median) is explained by guided EPS accretion only from 2028 (i.e. dilution through 2027) and suspended buybacks (8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315293/000119312526375328/d108801dex991.htm; fact sheet Valuation). The evaluation's base basis treats this 'EV/EBITDA near peer median, earnings discount explained by dilution' split, with dilution offsetting the 18.5% TTM FCF margin, as the modal (highest-probability) outcome.

bear.probability_evidence: Net debt/EBITDA is already 2.50x TTM before the ~$17.0bn all-debt USI deal, FCF conversion has fallen from 162.9% (FY2021) to 83.0% TTM, and Altman Z is 1.67 (fact sheet Quality/Other). The macro overlay's dominant chain -- rising 10y Treasury yield (5.27%, +0.72pp/3m) and widening US HY credit spread (3.03%, +0.35pp/1m) raising the coupon AON locks in on the new USI debt -- tilts bear, moderate (research/AON/2026-10-08-macro.md macro_tilt); the evaluation's bear basis states the probability was raised from 0.25 to 0.35 for that tilt.

expected_12m_move.cite: mc-inputs.json factor_news.SPY headlines are mixed as of 2026-10-06/07: record highs led by big tech ('Combined Assets in SPY, SPYM Cross $1 Trillion', 'S&P 500 Hits Record High as Big Tech Leads') alongside breadth/risk warnings ('SPY, QQQ Pressured by Tech Selloff and Elevated Treasury Yields', 'Two big bearish trades point to skepticism', 'powered by tech-and not much else'); the macro overlay (research/AON/2026-10-08-macro.md) addresses rates/credit, not the broad equity factor directly. Per house rule, mixed/silent news -> 0.

Macro overlay (research/AON/2026-10-08-macro.md): 10y Treasury yield 5.27% (+0.49pp/1m, +0.72pp/3m) and 10y real yield (DFII10) 2.91% (+0.48pp/1m, +0.61pp/3m) are rising, driven almost entirely by real yield not inflation expectations, with the 2s10s curve steepening to ~0.48pp from ~0.36pp three months ago -- a 'less-dovish near-term pricing' chain that implies continued downward pressure on 7-10y Treasury (IEF) prices; corroborated by mc-inputs.json factor_news.IEF headlines ('US 30-Year Yields Return to 2002 High', 'The Bond Rout Is Deepening Even as Oil Tankers Return to the Strait of Hormuz', 'Global Bond Markets Sell Off on France's Fiscal Worries'). Kept modest (-4%, within the +-15% bound) given one IEF headline shows a partial yield retreat on a cooler PCE print.
